abstract: A rational Diophantine septuple is a set of seven nonzero rationals with 1 + xy a square for every pair; none is known. We release the sign: sets of nonzero rationals with 1 - xy = +-square for every two members, a mixed D(1)/D(-1) system whose all-plus case is the original problem (after multiplication by i, these are Diophantine tuples over Q(i) with members in iQ). We construct infinitely many rational septuples of the mixed system from pairs (a,c) that are at once Pythagorean, c^2 - a^2 = +-b^2, and Eisenstein, a^2 + ac + c^2 = k^2, and determine their signs exactly: fifteen of the 21 conditions are + and six are -, the minus signs forming a K4 on four members, each forced by the arithmetic of the curve (the sign of a join is the square class of acX(P), and the base triple has sign pattern (+,-eps,eps) for every such pair). So this mechanism lands exactly six signs away from a rational Diophantine septuple, and says where. For every such pair the triple {(a^2+c^2)/(ac), c^2/(a(a+c)), a^2/(c(a+c))} solves the mixed system; its curve is Y^2 = X(X+a^4)(X+c^4), on which S = (-a^2c^2, a^2c^2(c^2-a^2)) has order four and R = (ack^2, ack(a+c)(a^2+c^2)) infinite order, and three explicit identities give, for all but finitely many m, the septuple {rho_1,rho_2,rho_3} u {r(Q_0+2mR+jS): j=0..3}, Q_0 = R+(0,0). The pairs are the rational points of the elliptic quartic k^2 = 3m^4+n^4, infinitely many: (3,5), (-56,65), (-1425,2993), ... For (3,5), the triangles (3,4,5) and (3,5,7), the first layer is {34/15, 25/24, 9/40, 2143479/1115560, 2059200/4669921, 2113225/1145814, -137344/15}, whose reflection in the strong member 25/24 is exactly the septuple of rStation Paper 21 read over Q: a rational septuple of the mixed system with fifteen plus and six minus signs.

title: Rational septuples of the mixed system 1 - xy = +-square: infinitely many from Pythagorean-Eisenstein pairs, with exactly six forced minus signs
